title: Site-wide robotic stoppage with AGV synchronization loss
user_facing_summary: Use this response pattern when operators report that robots or AGVs are stopped, nothing is moving, the small sort is not running, or the robotic system is not responding. Confirm the scope and observable system state, investigate service and application health, restore the named robotic service or gateway through an approved procedure, correct residual AGV synchronization issues, and validate API and operational recovery.
playbook_goal: Restore stable robotic and sort operation by distinguishing a site-wide control-system or service interruption from a localized AGV condition, then validating service responsiveness, AGV state, and resumed automated operation.
observed_entry_symptoms: Operators reported that nothing was moving.
The robotic system was reported as not responding.
The small sort was not running.
Multiple bots were reported as not moving in different areas.
Totes could not be removed from the hospital workflow.
The RMS/HMI appeared mostly blank and displayed a message reported as '.NET Control not created.'
AGVs were reported as out of sync.
negative_or_absent_signals: The site initially reported no known failed AGV or visible AGV fault.
The source does not confirm that the apparent RMS message represented a specific root cause.
The source does not confirm that memory usage caused the service or application failure.
A successful HTTP response did not eliminate the API client's schema validation warning.
tentative_internal_patterns: Possible OptiSweep service termination or restart condition
Possible WCSWebApplication or related application fault
Possible AGV synchronization or roster-state inconsistency after service recovery
Possible Ignition gateway availability or performance concern
internal_pattern_notes: These are tentative evidence-derived patterns for retrieval, review, and future enrichment only. The packet supports service termination and application-error observations, but it does not establish a single confirmed root cause. Memory behavior was reviewed and was not reported as indicating that memory caused the crash.
affected_systems_or_components: Windows Event Viewer / Service Control Manager
confidence_reason: The packet contains direct source artifacts and case comments covering the symptom pattern, Event Viewer evidence, service recovery, RMS AGV correction, API validation, and operational recovery. Exact recovery commands and the definitive causal chain are intentionally not inferred.

nodes.title: Confirm the observable scope of the stoppage
nodes.intent: Determine whether the report represents a site-wide or broad robotic stoppage with abnormal control-system presentation rather than an isolated robot issue.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the report represents a site-wide or broad robotic stoppage with abnormal control-system presentation rather than an isolated robot issue.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to ask the site which affected areas or workflows are stopped, whether multiple robots are stationary, and whether automated sorting or hospital tote removal is affected; also inspect the RMS/HMI overview for a normally populated versus mostly blank operational display and any readable system or AGV error indicators.
nodes.source_supported_description: The incident began with reports that nothing was moving, the small sort was not running, and the robotic system was not responding; RMS screenshots showed an abnormal mostly blank presentation.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to ask the site which affected areas or workflows are stopped, whether multiple robots are stationary, and whether automated sorting or hospital tote removal is affected; also inspect the RMS/HMI overview for a normally populated versus mostly blank operational display and any readable system or AGV error indicators.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator or support user confirms through site interview and the RMS/HMI view whether multiple robots or areas are stopped, the small sort or hospital workflow is affected, and the RMS page is populated normally. Unhealthy signals are broad non-movement, robotic-system nonresponse, or a mostly blank RMS page with an apparent '.NET Control not created.' message. Healthy signals are localized impact with otherwise normal fleet presentation. Inconclusive signals are an unclear scope report, unreadable RMS display, or unavailable site confirmation.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: RMS screenshots show ACB System 1 - RMS with a mostly blank panel and an apparent '.NET Control not created.' message; page 5.
Case comments and Teams messages record site reports that nothing was moving, the robotic system was not responding, and hospital totes could not be removed; pages 2 and 25.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet contains a site-wide stoppage report and a blank RMS/system-status presentation.

healthy_indicators: Site reports only a localized issue.
RMS overview is populated and shows normal system presentation.
Other automated areas continue operating.
unhealthy_indicators: Multiple areas or robots are stopped.
Nothing is moving or the robotic system is not responding.
Small sort or hospital workflow is unavailable.
RMS main panel is mostly blank or shows the apparent '.NET Control not created.' message.
inconclusive_indicators: Only one robot is reported stopped.
The RMS image or error sections cannot be read.
The site cannot confirm whether the stoppage is broad or localized.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: If the scope cannot be confirmed or the evidence is limited to an unreadable interface, leave this path for retriage rather than assuming a system-wide service fault.

nodes.goal: Determine whether Windows evidence indicates an OptiSweep service termination or clustered WCSWebApplication/application errors that correlate with the broad stoppage.

Healthy signals are no relevant service termination or clustered application errors. Inconclusive signals are unavailable logs, ambiguous timestamps, or errors without a credible temporal relationship to the stoppage.

nodes.intent: Confirm that the recovered control path responds before attempting residual AGV correction or releasing the site to automated operation.
nodes.goal: Confirm that the recovered control path responds before attempting residual AGV correction or releasing the site to automated operation.

nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1, L2, or L3 support checks the named OptiSweep/WCS API and, where applicable, the Ignition Systems Overview and Windows Services state. Healthy signals are a successful GetAgvStatuses response with returned AGV records, an available gateway status page, and a Running OptiSweep service. Unhealthy signals are no API response, unavailable gateway, or a stopped or repeatedly failing service. Inconclusive signals are HTTP success with unclear data validity, such as the observed schema warning, or a status page without confirmation of current service responsiveness.

nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator confirms that automated movement and the affected sort workflow have resumed, while support confirms service/API responsiveness and no residual out-of-sync AGVs in the available status views. Healthy signals are resumed auto bag-out or automated operation, normal or coherent AGV status, and continued service responsiveness. Unhealthy signals are renewed non-movement, inability to complete the affected workflow, repeated service termination, or residual AGV synchronization issues. Inconclusive signals are only a service-running display, a single HTTP 200 response with unresolved data ambiguity, or recovery of one workflow without confirmation of broader operation.
